title: The Dollar Pocket Watch and the Safety Pin: The Equality of Time
summary: When a wealthy visitor offered him a luxury gold watch, Gandhi asked whether a gold watch counted 65 seconds in a minute, reminding him that time is the universal equalizer.
keywords: The Dollar Pocket Watch and the Safety Pin: The Equality of Time
full_text:
Among Mahatma Gandhi's meager physical possessions, none was more iconic than his nickel-plated Ingersoll pocket watch, suspended from the waistband of his dhoti by an ordinary steel safety pin.

Gandhi was famously rigorous about punctuality. To him, wasting another person's time was a form of theft.

One afternoon at Sevagram Ashram, an affluent visitor observed Gandhi checking his watch. The guest noticed the tarnished metal casing and the humble safety pin.

Flicking open his own gleaming Swiss gold chronometer, the visitor said:
"Bapu! You are the foremost leader of Asia. It pains me to see you wearing a battered one-dollar timepiece fastened with a rusted safety pin. Allow me to present you with a solid gold wristwatch as a gift!"

Gandhi turned to the visitor with a serene smile:
"My friend! Tell me: how many seconds does your solid gold watch register in one minute?"

The visitor replied in confusion: "Why, sixty seconds, Bapu."

Gandhi pulled out his humble dollar watch:
"Behold: this nickel watch also registers precisely sixty seconds in a minute! Your gold watch does not grant sixty-five seconds to a rich man, does it?
Time is nature's supreme democrat: it grants precisely the same twenty-four hours to the beggar on the street and the emperor on his throne!
What matters is not whether the watch is encased in gold, but whether we fill those precious seconds with selfless service to suffering humanity!"

The visitor bowed his head in humility.

Gandhi added: "Sell your gold watch, my friend, and donate the proceeds to dig a well for the villagers; that will be far more pleasing to my heart!"
moral: Time is life's most precious and democratic gift; the value of a moment lies in how honorably we spend it.
witty_quote: Does your gold watch grant sixty-five seconds to a minute for the rich? Time treats the pauper and the prince with absolute equality!
